<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **144** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json a7199ef9744edf0c3ef0e381bb95a328545a3da9` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `9bdfc8677ae2f6792e880c7e891d1f224e213654` — the merge of head `56cac787cbe56defaa3853fd178e7865bf6ea889` into base `a7199ef9744edf0c3ef0e381bb95a328545a3da9`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 9bdfc8677ae2f6792e880c7e891d1f224e213654 && git checkout 9bdfc8677ae2f6792e880c7e891d1f224e213654
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin a7199ef9744edf0c3ef0e381bb95a328545a3da9 56cac787cbe56defaa3853fd178e7865bf6ea889 && git checkout -B drift-repro a7199ef9744edf0c3ef0e381bb95a328545a3da9 && git merge --no-ff 56cac787cbe56defaa3853fd178e7865bf6ea889

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json a7199ef9744edf0c3ef0e381bb95a328545a3da9
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs a7199ef9744edf0c3ef0e381bb95a328545a3da9` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **`DroppedFieldsEvent.reason` gains `stored_expression` (widening, right).** `data-engine.zod.ts` closes `reason` over five values in the stated order; the spec pin test asserts the exact five-tuple and still rejects an unknown string. The `fields` and schema describes now cover a field written with the computed value, which is what distinguishes it from `computed` (key dropped, nothing written). The name follows the field-role register of `primary_key` / `computed`, as the describe argues. Right.
2. **Emit on insert, batch, `insertMany` per-row, update by id, predicate update, only when the caller's value differs (right).** `replacedStoredExpressionFields` requires three facts: the key is on the entry snapshot (`suppliedPerRow` / `suppliedValues`, both pre-existing on `main`, taken from `opCtx.data` before hooks), the key is still on the payload the compute pass reads (so a value the `readonly` / `readonly_when` strip took is reported once under that reason, confirmed by the test at line 191), and the stored value differs by `Object.is` on at least one row. Insert: computed per live row, filtered against `insertDroppedPerRow`, carried into the batch union and the per-row `droppedFields` of `insertMany`. By id: compared against the one computed row. Predicate: compared against every matched row merged with the settled patch, so a patch that moves no input (column left alone) still reports a differing caller value, and the equal-value control reports nothing. Tests cover each path with an equal-value and an unsent-value control. Right.
3. **Not refused under `strictReadonlyWrites` in 18.x (right, per 「甲」).** Insert: the strict throw now judges `refusableInsertDrops` (computed + readonly only) at the exact point it stood on `main`, before the computation; the listener then fires for the full `insertDrops`, which under strict can only hold `stored_expression`. Update paths: a new listener-only `notifyDrop` carries the report, and `emitDrop` (strict-or-listener) is untouched for the four refusable reasons. In the head file `assertNoStrictDrops()` sits at 18096 and the by-id `notifyDrop` at 18109; on the predicate path 18380 then 18397. So a refused write never fires the listener, and the test at line 281 pins it (refused for `readonly_when` alone, nothing written, no events). `readonly-strict-errors.ts` gains only the `REASON_PHRASE` row its exhaustive key type demands; no refusal is built with it. The `WriteObservabilityOptions` TSDoc names `stored_expression` as the one arm outside strict coverage for 18.x, which keeps the "derived coverage" contract honest instead of silently contradicting it. Right.
4. **Exhaustive consumers over `reason` (all covered).** At the head, `git grep` finds two `Record` tables keyed by the union: objectql `REASON_PHRASE` (row added) and service-automation `DROPPED_REASON_LABEL` (row added, and `droppedFieldsWarning` says "value(s) were NOT stored ... succeeded with the computed value(s)" for this reason instead of the "NOT written ... without them" sentence that would be false of a written field; pinned by `crud-dropped-fields.test.ts`). `READONLY_CLASS_REASONS` (a `ReadonlySet`) and `protocol.ts`'s `byKey` map are non-exhaustive and need no row. objectui `STRIPPED_LINE` at the pin `cf153eb2e535` is keyed by `DroppedFieldsEvent['reason'] | 'stored_expression'` and carries the `stored_expression` row (`writeWarningToast.ts:145`, `:173`), so it type-checks against the spec both before and after this PR. TypeScript Type Check and Type Check · consumer gates are success on the head.
5. **Generated references** (`content/docs/references/**`): regenerated text only, in line with the new describes. The PR body's acceptance notes name the two things this review also sees and that are outside the card's surface: an `Object.is` type mismatch (a `Date` against an ISO string) would be reported, and the `/batch`, protocol and `ImportRowResult` "LEGALLY strips" prose is now one reason short. Neither blocks: the first is a report, not a refusal, and the second is describe drift.

### ② Semver level

Changeset `.changeset/24690-stored-expression-dropped-fields.md`: `@objectstack/spec` minor, `@objectstack/objectql` minor, `@objectstack/service-automation` patch. A new value on a published payload enum is an additive widening, so spec minor is right; objectql publishes a new event value on `onFieldsDropped` / `droppedFields`, minor is right; service-automation changes only a label row and a warning sentence, patch is right. No BREAKING marker and no ADR-0087 marker, which matches the re-scoped head (the strict refusal is out).
